$comment: Target profile for common mullein, an introduced Eurasian biennial. A dry-ground plant: it wants sparse, sunny, well-drained disturbed ground and is crowded out of lush meadow, so this is the first profile that uses an NDVI ceiling (ndvi.hard_max) as well as a floor. Harvesting an invasive is welcome; that does not change land-status rules.
habitat_note: Introduced from Eurasia; listed as invasive in BC. Dry, sunny, gravelly or sandy disturbed ground in the valleys: road shoulders, rail grades, gravel pits, burns, river terraces and dry open pine / fir forest. Rosettes need bare soil to establish, so it thins out as ground cover closes. Rarely above ~1,100 m here.

terrain_subweights.$comment: Elevation separates the warm valleys from everything else, and warm aspects matter for a dry-site plant.

observations.$comment: 111 AOI records, overwhelmingly on roadsides: the access bias here is real habitat, not just collector bias, because mullein genuinely follows roads. Other Verbascum (moth mullein V. blattaria) share the habitat and keep the default 'other' weight.

elevation_m.$comment: Records: p05 446 m, median 549 m, p95 1063 m.

aspect.$comment: Warm, dry exposures: SSW with +-70 deg full credit.

ndvi.$comment: Sparse ground: a floor low enough for gravel shoulders and a ceiling that falls away on lush, closed sward where rosettes cannot establish.

logging.$comment: Neutral: mullein colonises landings, skid trails and burned blocks.

validation.$comment: Yarrow is recorded by the same people on the same roadsides but spans every elevation and moisture level; beating it means the model is picking out warm, dry, sparse valley ground.
